{
  "verdict": "fix",
  "issues": [
    "GET /v1/tasks returns an unbounded array without pagination, filtering, or sorting parameters, creating scalability and performance risks.",
    "The PATCH endpoint lacks a specified patch format (e.g., RFC 7396 JSON Merge Patch or RFC 6902 JSON Patch), leaving client implementation ambiguous.",
    "String fields like 'title' and 'description' in request schemas lack length or pattern constraints, risking payload abuse and storage inconsistencies.",
    "The specification omits common HTTP status codes (401, 403, 409, 422) and does not clarify how the error schema maps to different failure scenarios.",
    "The 'id' field is defined only as a generic string without a format constraint (e.g., UUID), leaving client expectations and backend generation rules unspecified."
  ],
  "suggestions": [
    "Add query parameters for pagination (limit/offset or cursor) and basic filtering to the GET /v1/tasks endpoint.",
    "Explicitly declare the PATCH media type and format (e.g., application/merge-patch+json) to standardize partial update behavior.",
    "Enforce validation constraints such as maxLength, minLength, and regex patterns on all string inputs to ensure data integrity.",
    "Document additional relevant status codes (401, 403, 409, 422) and define a consistent error response structure that clearly maps codes to the error schema.",
    "Specify the ID format (e.g., format: 'uuid') and explicitly state that IDs are server-generated upon creation."
  ]
}
